column1: # The counted classes of tools/audit-type-system.sh, and the number each one is allowed to have.
# This is a **ratchet**: the gate measures each class over production code (test blocks stripped,
# comments and string literals removed) and compares the measurement to the number here in *both*
# directions. A rise fails the build until the baseline is raised deliberately in the same commit; a
# fall fails it until the baseline is lowered. Neither direction is a warning, because a number that
# can move without a commit saying so is a number nobody is watching — the same rule the coverage
# floor uses (`tools/audit-test-register.sh`, `floor(measured) - 2`).
# Measured 2026-09-26 by the gate itself (`bash tools/audit-type-system.sh`), at `6b7a7f494`+C98;
# `cast` and `div` re-measured and reviewed the same day at `1078a824c` (see the paragraph below).
# Regenerate by running the gate after a change: it prints the measured value in the FAIL message.
# Two of these classes did not exist before that date. The audit pass of 2026-09-26 found the gate's
# scope to be panic/unsafe/silent/escape (hard) and cast/lax/get (soft, printed, never compared), so
# **variable indexing, slice ranges and division had no class at all** and overflow existed only as
# clippy's opinion — while `spec/TYPE-SYSTEM.md` §1.6's "no silent partiality" is the claim this gate
# is cited as enforcing. The counts are large because the classes are legal Rust; what is not legal is
# one *arriving unremarked*.
# `get` is 0 as of the split: its pattern used to carry `\b[a-zA-Z_]+\[[0-9]+\]` alongside the
# accessor form, and that alternative was all of it (measured: accessor half 0, index half 95 of 95).
# The index half is the `index` class now, counted properly at 313 rather than at the 95 that a
# literal-index-only pattern could see.
# **`cast` 332→336 and `div` 49→50, reviewed 2026-09-26 — the five sites are not this pass's.** They
# arrived with the merge of PR #67 (`016989af6`), *after* the measurement above, so the ratchet has
# been failing at step 1 of `test & coverage` on every commit since C98 — the register gate, the test
# suite and the coverage floor never ran behind it, which is how a green-looking audit series carried
# a red job. Each site, reviewed rather than waved through:
#   casper/src/merging.rs:515,541  `guard.len() as u64`            — `usize` → `u64` is *widening* on
#   casper/src/merging.rs:539      `pruned as u64`                   every target the node builds for,
#   casper/src/merging.rs:633      `elapsed().as_millis() as u64`    and the values are the
#                                                                    `Relaxed` observability counters
#                                                                    of the block-index cache (read
#                                                                    back at `:978`). The millis one is
#                                                                    a `u128` → `u64` narrowing, and
#                                                                    truncating it needs ~584 million
#                                                                    years of replay; it is a
#                                                                    diagnostic that never reaches
#                                                                    consensus.
#   node/src/runtime/node_runtime.rs:639  `stats.calls % 250`      — a log throttle: a counter modulo
#                                                                    a non-zero literal. The `div` class
#                                                                    flags it because a regex cannot
#                                                                    judge intent, which is the case
#                                                                    for a human reading it.
# Raise rather than fix, deliberately: the fix would be to rewrite another PR's freshly merged
# diagnostics from inside an audit unit, and would swap `as u64` for `try_from(..).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)`
# — a silent saturation in a metric, which is worse than the cast it replaces. The doctrine above is
# that these classes are legal Rust and what is *not* legal is a site **arriving unremarked**; this
# paragraph is the remark. `overflow` stays 41: the pass's own arithmetic (AUDIT C100's depth walk) is
# written `saturating_add`, so it adds no site — a ratchet is for sites someone reviewed, and that one
# needs no review.
# class
cast
lax
get
